blocks.text: Why this choice is correct

In an unsorted array, a value smaller than `a[mid]` can occur on either side of mid, and so can a larger value. A mismatch therefore proves only that mid is not the target; discarding either side can discard the answer.

Complexity ranks correct algorithms; it cannot repair an invalid elimination rule.

blocks.text: A cost model must include every lifecycle phase. Define P[0] = 0 and build P[i + 1] = P[i] + a[i] for all n values, which costs O(n) time. blocks.text: How to reason it out

Fix the word width and write nonzero x as P·1·0^k, where the shown 1 is its lowest set bit. Two's-complement negation complements every bit and adds one. Complementing gives NOT P·0·1^k; adding one carries through the k trailing ones and produces NOT P·1·0^k. Above the shown 1, P and NOT P cannot both contain 1 in the same position; at and below it, both words contain exactly 1·0^k. Their AND is therefore 0…0·1·0^k, a one-hot mask.

items: Example in 8 bits: x = 10110000.
NOT x = 01001111, so -x = 01010000 after adding one.

blocks.text: x AND -x isolates the lowest set bit only under a declared finite-width two's-complement bit model. For x = 0 it returns 0 rather than a real one-hot bit.

messages.text: Above the lowest 1, x and -x have complementary bits; those positions cannot survive AND together.
The complement-and-add-one carry stops at the lowest 1, not the highest 1, so the shared position is determined from the right.
Every nonzero finite bit pattern has a rightmost 1, and that position is 1 in both x and -x.
